title: kith-store: negative i64 timestamps silently wrap to large u64 values
description: Timestamp columns (created_at, delivered_at, read_at, first_seen_at, last_seen_at, last_message_at) are stored as i64 but cast directly to u64 via "x as u64" in row_to_message, row_to_chat, row_to_contact. No CHECK constraint enforces non-negativity. A negative value (clock skew, test data, corruption) wraps to a huge u64 (~500M years CE) and produces a nonsensical RFC 3339 timestamp with no error. Same pattern as size_bytes which already has an explicit IntegralValueOutOfRange check. Fix: add .max(0) guards or explicit error returns for negative timestamps, consistent with the size_bytes pattern.
